scope: Proposition 5.3 (Independent-root comparison) of the manuscript “The joint Dickman law for consecutive integers” (preprints/The-joint-Dickman-law-for-consecutive-integers-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 012 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e66b4e8a1fe197d3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 39-40. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Mik(Si, Sk; s) be a symmetric real kernel, zero on nonpairs, with total absolute mass O(B10) uniformly in its arguments. Then Eu Kk−i(u + i, s) − Mik(Si(u), Sk(u); s)  i,k □ ≤ o(1) + E(Si) indep Lik(Si, Sk; s) − Mik(Si, Sk; s)  i,k □ . (5.10) 39 The error is uniform for s ∈ S.
